description: Titanium is a chemical element with symbol Ti and atomic number 22. Found in nature only as an oxide, it is a lustrous transition metal with a silver color, low density, and high strength. It is resistant to corrosion in sea water, aqua regia, and chlorine.
uses: Titanium alloys are used in aerospace including jet engines, missiles, and spacecraft, as well as military, industrial processes, automotive, agriculture, sporting goods, jewelry, and consumer electronics. Titanium is also highly biocompatible and used in medical applications including prostheses, orthopedic implants, dental implants, and surgical instruments. Titanium dioxide is used as a photocatalyst and in white pigments, while titanium tetrachloride is used in smoke screens and catalysts, and titanium trichloride is used as a catalyst in polypropylene production.
characteristics: Titanium is recognized for its high strength-to-weight ratio, being as tensile-strong as some steels but less dense, with a melting point of 1,668 °C. It is paramagnetic with low electrical and thermal conductivity compared to other metals, and forms a protective thin oxide layer upon air exposure that provides excellent corrosion resistance. The metal is ductile, especially in oxygen-free environments, and has the highest tensile-strength-to-density ratio of any metallic element.
